# stickfin / "Anti Broke" channel — reference for AI tools

This file exists so any AI assistant picking up this repo — a fresh Claude
session, another tool, whatever — has the context that took real
trial-and-error across multiple sessions to establish, without re-deriving
it from scratch or repeating fixes already made (or mistakes already
caught) once.

## READ THIS FIRST: the channel's live identity is the cinematic pipeline, on `test`

Everything below this section (character library, flat-vector props, the old
"Starting a new chat" callout) describes the pipeline as it stood through
2026-09-16, on `main`. As of 2026-09-17 (`b3181de`, memory:
project-cinematic-pivot) the channel's actual identity is a full-bleed
photoreal-cartoon cinematic style with two locked recurring characters,
Sarah and Mike — and it ONLY exists on the `test` branch, which was never
merged into `main`. If you're picking up this repo fresh and `main`/this
worktree doesn't have `assets/cinematic_cast/`, you are looking at the
PAUSED pipeline — check `git log --all --oneline | grep -i cinematic` and
switch to (or branch off) `test` before doing any real channel work. See
"## Cinematic pipeline (current, `test` branch)" further down for the full
current workflow, including how to do a "style-remake" request (recreate a
reference reel's animation style/hook formula with our own characters and
original narration) end to end.

## Starting a new chat? Paste this to the new AI first

> I'm continuing work on "Anti Broke" (stickfin), an autonomous personal-finance
> Shorts channel. Read `llms.txt` at the repo root first, in full — it has the
> architecture (also see README.md/SETUP.md) and everything fixed across every
> session so far. Three things matter most before you touch anything:
> 1. The channel's LIVE identity is the cinematic pipeline (Sarah/Mike,
>    full-bleed photoreal-cartoon scenes) and it only exists on the `test`
>    branch — `main` still has the older, paused flat-vector pipeline. Check
>    which one you're actually looking at first. See "## Cinematic pipeline
>    (current, `test` branch)" below.
> 2. (Flat-vector / `main` only) Character art is a FIXED pose library
>    (unchanged, never regenerate it live) — props/pictures are per-video
>    Nano Banana generations, either flat-vector (default) or photorealistic
>    (`photoreal_props: true`). Read "Prop art" below before writing a script
>    with props, especially before using photoreal mode — a real, unguarded
>    generation returned a trademarked Patek Philippe watch and a fabricated
>    passport with a synthetic face and real airline branding on the first
>    attempt.
> 3. `.github/workflows/publish-now.yml` and `upload-longform.yml` had a
>    shell-injection bug that silently stripped every `$` from a video's
>    title/description on the live post (fixed in an earlier session) — see
>    "CI: title/description shell injection" below. The first two videos
>    published before the fix likely still have corrupted descriptions live
>    on YouTube/IG/TikTok; nobody has gone back to re-edit those posts yet.
> Once you've read the whole file, tell me what you understand the current
> state to be, then I'll tell you what I want to do today.

## Cinematic pipeline (current, `test` branch) — style-remake workflow

**Everything else in this file describes the PAUSED flat-vector pipeline.**
As of 2026-09-17 the channel's live identity is the cinematic pipeline —
Pixar/DreamWorks-grade photoreal-cartoon scenes, one full-bleed AI-generated
scene per beat (the character IS the scene, no separate cutout/compositing
layer), Ken Burns push-in on every scene-only shot, hard cuts roughly every
5s. It exists ONLY on `test`. Multiple worktrees may already have `test`
checked out (`git worktree list` to check) — branch off it instead of
fighting over the checkout: `git checkout -b <name> test`.

### Locked characters — identity lock is TEXT-driven, not automatic
Two canonical cross-video reference images, reused by every script, never
regenerated: `assets/cinematic_cast/sarah.png` (navy three-piece suit, red
tie, long dark hair — the recurring host) and `assets/cinematic_cast/mike.png`
(charcoal three-piece suit, short dark hair — second character, redesigned
mid-project to be racially-ambiguous/curly hair/sharp jaw). A script's
`cast:` block still needs a `look:` string per character (schema requires
it, and it's the fallback if the canonical PNG is ever missing), but once
the canonical file exists it's barely used — what actually matters is the
scene `bg:` prompt TEXT: `assets.py`'s identity-lock only attaches a
character's reference image to a scene if that character's NAME appears
(word-boundary regex) somewhere in that scene's own `bg:` text. Forgetting
to literally write "Sarah" or "Mike" into a scene description silently
drops identity-lock on that one shot and the model free-invents a face.

### Style-remake requests ("recreate this reel's style with our characters")
Confirmed working end-to-end on a real 2026-09-21 session (see `bd3d384`,
"The House Nobody Wanted Made Her Rich" — a real-estate BRRRR story styled
after a reference IG reel, Sarah as the protagonist, fully original
narration):
- One `scenes.s_bNN.bg` per beat, script-level `cinematic: true`. Leave
  `beat.cast` empty — only the script-level `cast:` block plus the bg text's
  name-mention (above) matters for identity lock in cinematic mode.
- `caption_style: title` + `title_card:` set to the hook line reproduces a
  reference reel's "big bold centred hook text over the opening shot, then
  word-by-word reveal captions after" formula almost exactly — this is the
  existing "title" caption style, nothing new needed.
- **Color grade has no global config knob.** There's no
  `config.COLOR_GRADE` or per-script palette field. To lock in a specific
  look (e.g. the hyper-vibrant/saturated/high-contrast "deep blue sky, warm
  golden sunlight" grade requested and confirmed working this session),
  write that language directly into EVERY scene's `bg:` prompt alongside
  the framing/action description — repeat it beat to beat, don't assume it
  carries over. `CINEMATIC_STYLE` in assets.py is a shared floor (dual-tone
  lighting, no sterile/plain-white sets) but does not encode any specific
  per-video palette on its own.
- A long-form "story" Short (90-120s, ~20-25 beats, one clear visual per
  beat) is legitimate and was the actual target this session, not a
  mistake to trim down — see the QA gate note below.

### Pre-publish visual QA workflow — do this BEFORE the expensive full build
`assets_mod.plan_assets(script)` + `assets_mod.generate_assets(script, plan)`
generates every character/scene still WITHOUT touching TTS/render/mux —
cheap, fast way to review stills (especially hook/problem/payoff beats,
i.e. the ones a human would actually want to approve) before committing to
a full `tools.build_one` run. To force-regenerate one specific still after
a bad generation, delete just that one cached PNG
(`build/<slug>/assets/bg/s_bNN.png`) and re-run `generate_assets` — it
skips anything that already exists, so this only touches the deleted file.
Two real AI-generation defect classes hit this session, both fixed by
tightening the scene prompt text and regenerating, not by code changes:
- **Garbled/duplicated incidental text** on a text-bearing prop — a document
  with one correct highlighted line but gibberish filler text elsewhere on
  the page, or a heading rendered twice. Fix: explicitly tell the prompt the
  REST of the page is blank/no other text, don't just ask for the one line
  you actually want.
- **Ground-texture tiling seams** on a paved/stone surface the model
  invented unprompted (not even in the original text). Fix: explicitly
  specify a smooth, continuous, unbroken surface.
Also run the Gemini critique (`qa.check(script, run_critique=True)`) before
publish, not just the objective checks — it caught a real authoring bug
this session (an on-screen prop read "$190,000" while the narration said
"$180,000", a genuine script mistake, not an AI-generation defect) that no
amount of eyeballing stills in isolation would have caught.

### Two pipeline bugs fixed this session (affect every future cinematic short)
- `stickfin/music.py`: mood selection mapped `caption_style == "title"` to
  "playful" background music. Wrong — `title` is the serious hook-card style
  used by narrative shorts generally (this video, the BNPL trap video, etc),
  not specifically a skit/banter format. Fixed to key off
  `caption_style == "skit"` instead and fall through to the already-computed
  tense/neutral signal otherwise (`_sections()`).
- `stickfin/qa.py`: the short-format QA gate hard-blocked anything over 90s,
  citing a stale "Instagram caps Reels at ~90s" comment. IG Reels support up
  to 3 minutes now; widened the ceiling to 180s after a genuinely
  in-spec 111s video got rejected for no real platform reason.

### Publishing off `test`
`media/<slug>.mp4` needs to exist on whatever branch
`gh workflow run publish-now.yml --ref <branch>` is pointed at — for
anything in the cinematic pipeline that's `test`, not `main`. Workflow:
build on a feature branch off `test` → once approved,
`git push origin <branch>:test` (fast-forward) → copy
`build/<slug>/<slug>.mp4` into `media/` → commit → push again → dispatch
the workflow with `--ref test`.

**Bug, fixed 2026-09-21: `-f description="one long string"` silently ships an
Instagram caption with no paragraph breaks.** Confirmed by the user on three
live posts in a row before it was caught — every caption read as one dense
wall of text with no blank lines between the hook/body/CTA/hashtags. Root
cause wasn't a code bug (`publish.py`'s `buffer_post()` passes `text` straight
through to Buffer's GraphQL API with no transformation, and the GH Actions env
var itself was confirmed intact with correct spacing) — it was simply that
every `-f description="..."` value handed to `gh workflow run` so far had been
typed as ONE continuous sentence-string with zero `\n` characters in it, so
there was never a real newline anywhere in the pipe for Buffer/Instagram to
render. **Fix: stop using `-f`/`-F` for `description` entirely.** Use
`gh workflow run publish-now.yml --ref test --json` and pipe in a JSON payload
built with `python -c "import json; print(json.dumps({...}))"` (or equivalent)
so `\n\n` paragraph breaks are properly embedded as real newline characters in
the JSON string, e.g.:
```
python -c "import json; print(json.dumps({'slug': SLUG, 'title': TITLE,
  'description': 'Hook line.\n\nBody sentence or two.\n\nFollow @antibrokee '
  'for daily money insights.\n\n#Tag1 #Tag2 #Tag3'}))" | \
  gh workflow run publish-now.yml --ref test --json
```
Write captions as real multi-paragraph text (hook → brief body → CTA →
hashtags, each its own paragraph) every time, not one run-on sentence.

### The default workflow now: user hands over a full script, verbatim
Confirmed as the preferred going-forward pattern 2026-09-21 ("I like this
workflow, make it I give script and you make video workflow") — distinct from
the style-remake workflow above (which starts from a reference reel's STYLE,
not its words). Here the user supplies the exact hook line and the full
narration text, in order, and expects it built and published close to
verbatim:
- Map each numbered narration line to one beat (`say:` = that line, lightly
  reworded ONLY for TTS flow if genuinely needed — a numbered list item with
  an internal colon/dash structure, like "First: X. Second: Y.", usually
  splits cleanly into one beat per sub-item instead of one giant beat, for the
  same one-clear-visual-per-scene reason the style-remake section gives).
- **Still fact-check any concrete, checkable claim** (a specific return
  percent, an expense ratio, a company's market share, a dollar figure) via
  WebSearch/WebFetch before building — this is non-negotiable regardless of
  which workflow produced the script, per the channel's own "keep it
  accurate" rule. Cross-reference against a SINGLE consistent same-day source
  where possible (e.g. stockanalysis.com for multiple tickers) rather than
  mixing snapshots from different dates, which is what produced the
  inconsistent-looking numbers this session had to reconcile on the ETF
  video. Correct stale/wrong figures rather than publishing them as given;
  note what changed and why in the build commit message. Purely qualitative/
  conceptual content (no verifiable external claim) doesn't need this step.
- If the script's framing conflicts with `themes.yaml` (forward-looking buy
  advice, a specific-security thesis), that's a real conflict to flag and get
  an explicit decision on BEFORE building — see memory:
  feedback-hot-stock-content-policy for the standing resolution (keep the
  framing if the user says so, fact-check hard, disclaim "not financial
  advice" in the caption). Don't silently rewrite the user's framing to fit
  the policy, and don't silently ignore the policy either.
- When asked to publish at a specific future clock time (not "now"): build,
  QA, commit, and push everything to `test` immediately, but hold the actual
  `gh workflow run publish-now.yml` dispatch. Schedule it with the `schedule`
  skill / `RemoteTrigger` tool (`action: "create"`, `run_once_at` in RFC3339
  UTC — convert the requested local time to UTC and re-verify current time
  via `date -u` right before computing it, don't trust a stale reference
  time), using the bridge environment for this project
  (`env_01Ggh42FW6USJM6mnnEZ95LP` as of this session — confirm via the
  `schedule` skill's environment list if it's ever renumbered) so the cloud
  agent's `gh` call runs with this machine's real GitHub auth. The routine's
  prompt must be fully self-contained (the cloud agent starts with zero
  conversation context) — give it the exact command to run, including the
  full JSON-payload description built the newline-safe way above, and tell it
  to verify all three platform post ids came back afterward rather than just
  trusting a clean exit code.

## Character art: fixed library, not per-video generation

**Resolved this session.** The previous session ended undecided between two
paths: keep hardening live per-video AI pose generation (Nano Banana on
Vertex), or switch to a fixed, pre-made character-art library reused across
every video. This session built and shipped the fixed-library path, and it
has held up well across two full builds + publishes:

- **Source**: ChatGPT image generation, NOT Vertex/Nano Banana, for character
  and icon art. Confirmed materially more consistent at holding a character's
  exact design (outfit, proportions, face construction) across a whole sheet
  of poses than Nano Banana was — that inconsistency was a big chunk of what
  made the live-generation approach fragile in the first place. The workflow:
  paste a prompt (asking for N poses of ONE character in a grid, on a flat
  magenta #FF00FF background, reference-locked to a previous sheet's image
  when adding to an existing character), get a sheet back, cut it with
  `tools/cut_stickers.py`.
- **The cutout problem and fix**: rembg (ML background segmentation, trained
  on real photos) doesn't understand a flat colour key — at anti-aliased
  edges it leaves a partial-alpha pixel that's still colour-blended toward
  magenta, which reads as a pink fringe/halo once composited onto anything
  else. `tools/cut_stickers.py` replaces it with a proper Vlahos-style chroma
  key: measure how much of a pixel's colour is explained by the background's
  magenta signature (`min(R,B) - G`, normalised against the sheet's own
  sampled background colour), then UNMIX that fraction out of the RGB to
  recover the true colour at every partial-alpha edge pixel. A second real
  bug this surfaced: a pastel-coloured subject (a piggy bank's pink body, on
  an early icon-sheet test) can score nearly as "background-like" as a real
  edge pixel by colour alone — fixed by gating on TOPOLOGY, not colour: only
  pixels connected all the way out to the sheet's border through other
  background-scored pixels count as background (`scipy.ndimage.label` +
  keep only border-touching components). An enclosed same-hue fill, walled
  off by the (very un-background-coloured) black ink outline around it,
  stays opaque regardless of how magenta-like its own colour is.
- **Library layout**: `assets/char_library/{host,second}/<pose-slug>.png`,
  cut via `tools/cut_stickers.py`'s `process_sheet()` — each pose tight-
  cropped to its OWN content bbox (not a shared/union box across poses; that
  was tried and reverted, see below), then upscaled to a uniform 1600px
  source height (`target_h=1600`) so every pose has the same head-to-feet
  pixel height regardless of gesture. Sheets are archived at
  `assets/char_library/sheets/*.png`.
- **32 poses per character now** (64 total), built up over three ChatGPT
  sheets each: 16 neutral/everyday (sit + stand + gesture), 8 negative-
  reaction (defeated/frustrated/embarrassed/sulking — added after the
  library's only negative options read as "annoyed", not "hurt"), 8
  upward-gesturing (added after Gemini QA caught a character gesturing
  sideways at their scene partner instead of the prop/chart rendering above
  their head — see layout section below for why "above" is the only correct
  direction now).
- **`stickfin/assets.py`'s pose loop tries the library FIRST**
  (`_library_pose(voice, state, tone, has_visual)`, keyed off voice —
  `Orus`→host, `Aoede`→second, set deterministically in `generate.py` — not
  off whatever name the model gave the character that script), and only
  falls back to a live Vertex generation call if the library directory
  doesn't exist for that voice. In practice this means ZERO Vertex image
  calls for character art on every video built this session — cost and
  defect-rate both dropped to ~nothing for this asset class specifically
  (props/icons/charts/backgrounds were already non-generative before this
  session; see below).

### Pose selection — read this before touching `_library_pose` in assets.py

A LOT of real bugs got fixed here, each confirmed on an actual build or an
actual Gemini QA critique before being called done. The short version: match
a beat's freeform "pose, expression" text to the closest of 32 fixed stills
via keyword tags, with three independent bias layers on top of raw keyword
overlap —

1. **Tone bias** (`tone == "negative"`): penalises poses tagged with
   positive-affect words (smile, confident, thumbs-up, etc.) and adds a small
   tie-break bonus toward the negative-reaction pose set, so a character
   doesn't stay smiling through a beat about something bad happening to
   them. The negative-pose set is a candidate REGARDLESS of the tone flag
   (not gated behind it) — the beat's own pose TEXT ("looking down,
   defeated") is finer-grained signal than that one binary flag, and gating
   lost real matches on beats that were textually obviously negative but
   didn't happen to carry the flag. What actually needs to be gated is
   individual ambiguous WORDS, not the whole pose set — `slumped-defeated`
   used to include the tag "down", which matched completely unrelated text
   ("gesturing OUT AND DOWN towards the viewer" on the warm closing CTA
   line) and put a sad pose on the channel's sign-off. Fix the word, not the
   gate.
2. **Visual-target bias** (`has_visual`, true when the beat has a prop or
   chart): any prop/chart always renders in the shared ASSET band ABOVE both
   characters' heads (see layout section), never beside them. Two poses in
   the original 16 — `stand-presenting-open-hand`, `stand-explaining-stern`
   — draw an open hand/pointing gesture extended SIDEWAYS at chest height;
   in this geometry that can only ever read as pointing at whichever OTHER
   CHARACTER is standing next to them, never at the prop/chart overhead.
   Caught live by Gemini's pose-resonance QA check on a real published video
   ("gesturing towards the male character" while talking about the calendar
   prop rendering above her). Fix: `_SIDEWAYS_TO_UPWARD` maps each sideways
   pose to a purpose-built upward equivalent (`present-up-open-hand-calm`,
   `finger-tap-point-up-serious`) by SUBSTITUTION after the scoring loop
   picks a winner, not by adding those upward poses into the scoring
   competition directly — an earlier attempt gave the upward poses an
   unconditional score bonus whenever `has_visual` was true, which also beat
   completely unrelated poses with zero real connection to "pointing"
   ("winces, looks away" landed on a pointing-up pose because the bonus beat
   every other pose's raw zero). Priority order matters: when a beat is
   BOTH negative-toned AND has_visual with no keyword match at all, tone
   wins the fallback-pool choice, not gesture direction — there's no
   negative+upward-gesturing pose in the library, and a warm/neutral upward
   pose on an explicitly bad beat is a worse mismatch than an on-emotion
   pose that happens to gesture sideways.
3. **Default-pool rotation**: a beat whose pose text matches NO keyword at
   all used to collapse onto one single hardcoded default pose — confirmed
   on a real build: 8 of 27 poses in one video (~30%) were literally
   identical. Now rotates deterministically (hashed on the state text, so
   still reproducible build-to-build) across a small pool of plausible
   defaults, separate pools for standing/sitting/negative/has_visual.

Two lower-level fixes worth knowing about if you're adding more tags:
- **Light stemming** (`_word_forms`): exact-string tag matching missed a lot
  of real hits ("gesturing" not matching a tag written as "gesture",
  "realizing" not matching "realize"). Handles -ing and plural -s suffixes
  only, not a real stemmer.
- **Score per matched SOURCE WORD, not per matched tag element**
  (`_match_count`): several tags list both a word and its -ing form (added
  before stemming existed, e.g. "show" AND "showing" both listed). Once
  stemming expands an input word to multiple forms, intersecting against a
  tag set containing BOTH forms double-counts one real match as two — this
  was enough to let a wrong-direction gesture pose outscore the correct one
  in one real case. Count one hit per distinct source word regardless of how
  many redundant forms exist on either side.

### Layout: fixed split-screen template for two-character shots

Also resolved this session, and it's the user's own hand-drawn spec (a
photographed sketch, not a text description): a shared ASSET band on top
(charts/headlines/props — `layout._DUO_ASSET_Y`), a per-character DIALOGUE
strip directly above each head (D1 left / D2 right — `layout._DUO_DIALOGUE_Y`
+ `duo_dialogue_anchor()`), then two mirrored, EQUAL-HEIGHT character slots
at the bottom (`layout._DUO_CHAR_Y` + `_DUO_LEFT_X`/`_DUO_RIGHT_X`). Replaces
the old dynamic two-hander template entirely for any short-format shot with
exactly 2 character layers (`layout.solve()` branches on this before
touching the general `_regions()` template logic at all).

Why: characters are fit by HEIGHT ALONE within their slot, not
`min(width, height)` like every other template's `_fit()`. Every pose in the
library shares the same 1600px source height, so height-first fitting alone
guarantees two different poses in the same shot render at truly identical
height — the old `min()` approach let a wide-armed pose lose to the width
constraint and render visibly SHORTER than a narrow pose in the identical
slot (confirmed: 600px vs 755px tall, same nominal region, no collision
involved). The character-slot width band (`_DUO_CHAR_Y` height chosen
specifically) is tuned to the single WIDEST pose in the whole library
(1207px @ 1600 tall, an arms-flung gesture) so even the worst-case pairing
never needs the collision-resolution fallback as a matter of course — verified
by sweeping every pose width in the library pairwise against the widest one.

Captions: `captions.py`'s "title" and "skit" caption styles now `\pos()` a
speaking beat's dialogue line into the speaker's own D-box
(`captions._duo_pos()`, keyed off `script.cast[beat.who].anchor` being
"left"/"right" AND the beat actually having exactly 2 characters in
`beat.cast` — a solo reaction beat, e.g. the closing CTA, renders in the old
centred template instead, and pinning its caption to a D-box that doesn't
exist on screen there would misplace it).

This ALSO resolves the "Fixed-zone layout idea" that a previous session
discussed but explicitly did not implement (see old NOT-implemented notes,
now removed since this IS that idea, built).

**Follow-up bug, found live on a published video**: `_duo_safe()` deliberately
reserves NO top caption space in duo mode (dialogue lives in the D-boxes, not
a shared top band) — correct for beats 2+, but wrong for beat 1 specifically
in `caption_style: title`, where the persistent title-card caption IS a
shared top-anchored element (MarginV=250) that competes with the beat-1
headline graphic (`_DUO_ASSET_Y` started at 0.08). A real short shipped with
the title card sitting on top of the headline text — invisible to
`layout.audit()` since it only checks composited PNG layers against each
other, never the burned-in ASS caption. Fixed with `_DUO_HEADLINE_Y0 = 0.25`,
a lower start used only for headline layers (which only ever appear on beat
1) in `_solve_duo`'s asset-band placement.

### Motion: characters hold still now

`config.IDLE_BOB_PX` default changed to `0` (was `6`) — user feedback:
characters should stay steady during a held shot, not sway. "Life" now comes
from pose variety across cuts (the default-rotation + tone/visual-aware
selection above) instead of continuous idle motion, which fits this
channel's existing hard-cut style (no Ken Burns/tweening anywhere else)
better anyway.

### Compositor: soft drop shadow under character/prop/chart/cutout layers

`config.LAYER_SHADOW` (default on) — each layer casts a blurred, offset,
blackened copy of its own alpha silhouette behind itself before the real
layer draws, giving the flat composite some depth instead of reading as
stickers pasted on a blank canvas. No camera motion, no background change —
stays inside the static-camera hard-cut style. Headline text and the
full-frame red "negative" vignette are excluded (a shadow under giant hook
text looked heavy; the vignette isn't a "sticker").

**ffmpeg gotcha, worth knowing if you touch `compositor.py`'s filter graph
again**: a labelled pad (`[s{idx}]`) CANNOT be used as the input to two
different filters without an explicit `split` first — feeding it to both the
shadow-derivation chain and the final visible overlay without splitting
silently dropped the visible layer entirely while the shadow still rendered
(confirmed by disabling the shadow and comparing frames — the character was
fully present with the shadow code removed, fully absent with it in, same
input assets). Fixed with `[s{idx}]split=2[s{idx}a][s{idx}b]` before the two
consumers.

### Image model: bumped to gemini-3.1-flash-image

`config.IMAGE_MODEL` default changed from `gemini-2.5-flash-image` to
`gemini-3.1-flash-image`, and `IMAGE_LOCATION` from `us-central1` to
`global` — 3.1 only serves at `location="global"`, confirmed working on this
project. 2.5-flash-image @ us-central1 is the known-good fallback if 3.1
ever regresses.

### QA: pose-resonance check added to the Gemini critique

`stickfin/qa.py`'s `_critique()` now hands Gemini an explicit
beat-id → exact-spoken-line manifest alongside the sampled stills (built
from `script.beats`, not left for Gemini to guess from the tiny burned-in
word-reveal caption fragment visible in each still — that fragment is only
2-3 words at that instant, not the whole line, and was too unreliable a
ground truth for this specific judgment). Asks it to flag BOTH directions on
every still: a bigger reaction than the line warrants (over-exaggerated) and
a flatter one than the line warrants (under-reacting) — a genuinely big line
still warrants a big pose, so it's not "flag all drama", it's "flag mismatch
between pose intensity and THIS line's actual intensity". New JSON field
`pose_resonance`, one line per still. This is how the has_visual gesture-
direction bug above was actually found — ran the check, it named the exact
beats and explained why.

## Prop art: per-video Nano Banana generation, illustrated OR photoreal

**Resolved a different session** (later than the character-library work
above, same overall direction of travel: keep character identity locked and
cheap, but stop the rest of the frame looking generic). Character art stays
on the fixed library, untouched — this section is only about props/pictures
in the shared asset band.

- **Why this changed**: the channel's ~34-name fixed icon vocabulary
  (`assets/icons/*.png`, `icons.py`) is generic and reused across every
  video regardless of topic — a Nike video and a Bitcoin video would both
  reach for the same generic `chart-down` icon. `stickfin/assets.py`'s prop
  loop now tries `icons.path(key)` first (unchanged, free, instant) but a
  script simply describing a prop in freeform prose that doesn't match a
  fixed icon name falls through to a live Nano Banana generation — which,
  written well, can be a real story-telling picture (e.g. two pizza boxes +
  a receipt + coins for the Bitcoin Pizza Day story) instead of a bare icon.
  A hand-written script controls this simply by NOT using the fixed icon
  vocabulary in its `props:` text.
- **`ink=True` bug (fixed)**: the prop-generation cutout call originally
  reused `ink=True` from the icon-BUILD tooling, which force-crushes any
  fill colour below luminance 190 to solid black. Fine for the hand-picked,
  pre-vetted icon set it was written for; it silently destroyed real colour
  on a fresh generation — a "shiny gold coin stack" prop came back as an
  unreadable solid-black blob. Fixed to `ink=False`, same as character poses
  (which never had this bug, for the same reason).
- **Style-reference fallback**: `sheets` (character reference sheets used as
  a style anchor) is usually EMPTY, because both channel characters use the
  fixed pose library and never generate a fresh reference sheet. Without a
  visual anchor, a prop generation leans on the text description alone and
  drifts toward a more rendered/realistic look than the flat-vector prompt
  asks for — this is the documented reason props moved to a fixed icon
  library in an even earlier session (see `icons.py`'s own docstring: "that
  was the weak spot (inconsistent, too realistic)"). Fixed by falling back
  to any single still already sitting in `assets/char_library/{host,second}/`
  as the style anchor when `sheets` is empty.
- **Solidity-checked retry**: props now get the same kind of retry loop
  poses already had (up to 2 attempts, re-nudged toward the flat style if the
  first came back too realistic, keeping whichever attempt scored better on
  `_solidity()`) — added because this path now carries real production
  weight (every prop in a hand-written script) instead of being a rare
  fallback nobody hit in practice.
- **Prompt STRUCTURE vs CONTENT — a real regression, caught by the user
  live**: fixing a run of broken/illegible generations (an over-specified
  calendar grid, an unreadable "trapdoor" composition) by simplifying the
  prompt accidentally simplified the wrong axis — it kept the sentence
  short (correct fix; asking for precise text/grids is what broke those two)
  but also dropped the explicit "rich picture, not a bare icon" instruction,
  so the next few regenerated props read as minimal icons again. These are
  independent concerns: keep the prompt SENTENCE simple (avoid stacking many
  separate clauses, avoid asking for precise on-image text/numeric layouts —
  image models are unreliable at both), but keep the CONTENT instruction
  explicitly pushing toward a full illustrated scene.
- **`photoreal_props: true`** (new top-level script field, `script_model.py`
  + `Script.photoreal_props`): switches the prop prompt from flat-vector-
  matching-the-characters to actual photorealistic photos, for a video where
  that reads better than the channel's usual doodle style (real objects —
  a watch, a plane, cash — vs. an abstract concept a doodle icon handles
  fine). Skips BOTH the icon library and the style-reference image in this
  mode (a cartoon reference fights a photoreal prompt instead of helping).
  **Real safety issue found on the first live generation, not hypothetically
  guarded against in advance**: an unguarded `"photorealistic photo of a
  Swiss watch"` prompt returned an exact, unmodified, brand-legible Patek
  Philippe design, and `"photo of a passport next to a boarding pass"`
  returned a fully fabricated ID document — a photoreal synthetic human
  face, an invented name/passport number/date of birth, and real British
  Airways livery on the boarding pass. This class of risk barely exists in
  flat-vector doodle mode (a cartoon rarely spontaneously reproduces a real
  trademark or renders a convincing fake ID) but is real and easy to hit in
  photoreal mode. The photoreal prompt template now explicitly requires
  generic/unbranded objects (invent a plain version of anything that would
  normally be branded) and explicitly forbids human faces/portraits and
  anything laid out like a real passport/ID/driver's licence. **Still
  requires a human (or agent) visually reviewing every photoreal prop before
  publish** — the prompt guard is necessary but a Nano Banana generation can
  still surprise you; this was caught by actually looking at the images, not
  by the prompt alone.

## CI: title/description shell injection in publish workflows (fixed)

`.github/workflows/publish-now.yml` and `upload-longform.yml` both spliced
`${{ inputs.title }}` / `${{ inputs.description }}` directly into a bash
`run:` script as raw text. GitHub performs that substitution BEFORE bash
executes, so any `$` in the value (every dollar figure this channel's videos
are about — "$5 billion", "$100") gets re-parsed as a shell variable
reference by the Actions runner's own shell and silently vanishes; an
embedded literal `"` in the value breaks the quoting outright and crashes the
whole step with a confusing `unrecognized arguments` error (this is what
actually surfaced it — a description containing `"Four easy payments"` plus
several dollar amounts crashed a real publish run). Fixed in both workflows
by passing title/description through `env:` vars and referencing them as
`"$TITLE"`/`"$DESCRIPTION"` in the script — normal bash variable expansion,
whose value is never re-interpreted as script syntax regardless of what
characters it contains.

**Known consequence, not yet fixed**: any video published via `Publish Now`
before this fix likely has its dollar amounts silently stripped from the
LIVE description on YouTube/Instagram/TikTok (Nike and Bitcoin Pizza Day,
specifically) — the bug doesn't crash on a plain `$` alone, only on an
embedded `"`, so those two went out looking successful. Re-editing those
live posts' captions hasn't been done — flagged to the user, no takedown/
repost policy decision made on it yet (see the "already-published videos are
left as-is" policy note below, though this is arguably different: not a new
finding about content quality, but a mechanical corruption of what was
actually posted vs. what was written).

## What this project does (see README.md and SETUP.md for full detail)

Daily-ish GitHub Actions cron: picks a personal-finance topic
(`themes.yaml`), writes a script (Gemini/Vertex), synthesizes TTS per beat,
resolves character art from the fixed pose library (falls back to live
Vertex/Nano Banana generation only if a character has no library — see
above), generates prop/chart/background art (icon library first, chart/
headline rendered locally with matplotlib/PIL, no API calls for either),
composites static shots with hard cuts (no Ken Burns/tweening), muxes audio +
captions, publishes to YouTube/Instagram/TikTok via Buffer.

Two formats: `short` (9:16, the daily output) and `wide` (16:9 long-form,
separate/less-used path — the fixed duo layout above is short-format only,
`wide` still uses the older dynamic two-hander template). Two script shapes:
`explainer` (one host, talks to camera) and `skit` (host + a second
character, back-and-forth dialogue) — the fixed split-screen layout and
per-character dialogue boxes only apply to a shot with exactly 2 characters
on screen, which in practice means skit format.

Publishing paths (`.github/workflows/`):
- `daily.yml` — manual-dispatch, full generate-through-publish, one video.
- `batch-build.yml` + `poster.yml` — the automatic cadence: batch-build N
  videos ahead into `state/queue.json`, poster.yml drains one per scheduled
  firing (4x/day), no Vertex call needed on the posting side. **Note: as of
  this session, both of these are dormant** — nobody has manually triggered
  `batch-build.yml` since 2026-09-01, so `state/queue.json` fully drained by
  2026-09-13 and `poster.yml` has been firing successfully on schedule with
  nothing to post ever since. This session's videos were built and published
  one at a time via `tools/build_one.py` (new this session — builds a
  specific already-written script end to end without spending another
  `generate()` call) + `publish-now.yml`, bypassing the queue entirely. The
  queue path needs a decision: wire `batch-build.yml` onto a real schedule
  now that the pose library makes each build cheaper (no Vertex image
  calls), or keep hand-building one at a time for now while pose selection
  is still actively being tuned.
- `publish-now.yml` — publish an already-committed `media/<slug>.mp4`
  immediately, bypassing the queue. This session's normal path: copy the
  local `build/<slug>/<slug>.mp4` to `media/`, commit + push, then
  `gh workflow run publish-now.yml -f slug=... -f title=... -f description=...`.

## Published on the new pipeline this session

- `2026-09-15-used-car-true-cost` — first video built entirely on the fixed
  pose library (16-pose version, old dynamic layout still active). Published
  live (YouTube/IG/TikTok via Buffer) before the layout/motion/pose-
  resonance fixes above, so it does NOT have the split-screen layout, steady
  characters, or the later pose-selection improvements.
- `2026-09-15-berkshire-hathaway-compounding-power` — first video with the
  fixed duo layout, per-character dialogue boxes, steady (no-bob)
  characters, and the improved (at-the-time) pose selection. Published live.
  The has_visual gesture-direction bug (fixed in `39dc801`/`5745532`) was
  found via Gemini QA critique run AFTER this video was already live.
- `2026-09-15-nike-lost-default-status` — hand-written (not
  `stickfin.generate`) one-off on a user-supplied topic; had to be rewritten
  from the user's original framing into strictly past-tense, sourced facts
  to stay inside `themes.yaml`'s no-forward-prediction rule. Published live.
  Likely has a corrupted (dollar-amounts-stripped) live description — see
  the CI section above.
- `2026-09-15-bitcoin-pizza-day` — hand-written; first video with per-video
  Nano Banana props instead of the fixed icon vocabulary (the `ink=True`
  colour-crush bug was found and fixed mid-build on THIS video's props).
  Published live. Also likely has a corrupted live description.
- `2026-09-16-buy-now-pay-later-trap` — hand-written, original topic; first
  video with a picture on every single beat (no bare talking-head shots) and
  the fixed beat-1 headline/title-card layout. Published live, description
  correct (built after the CI fix).
- `2026-09-16-swiss-watch-tariff` — hand-written; first video using
  `photoreal_props: true`. The user asked to adapt a competitor reference
  video's exact script — declined reproducing its specific dialogue/scenes
  (that's someone else's creative expression, not public-domain fact), and
  the reference's core factual claim ("an empty private jet skips customs
  scrutiny, letting buyers dodge duty on luxury goods") didn't hold up under
  a fact-check (no documented source; every private jet clears customs
  regardless of passenger count) — so the actual script covers a different,
  verified real story instead (the 2025-26 US tariff on Swiss goods hitting
  watch prices, real ~8.1% Swiss VAT / ~$800 US personal exemption figures,
  and the real, well-documented Lewis Hamilton VAT-avoidance jet-import
  case). Published live after the Patek Philippe / fake-passport safety
  issue (see "Prop art" section above) was caught and fixed pre-publish.

**Established policy, reconfirmed explicitly by the user again this
session**: already-published videos are left as-is when a bug/improvement
is found after the fact — fixes apply going forward only, no takedown/
repost, unless the user says otherwise for a specific case. All videos
listed above are still live with whatever issues are noted next to them.

## Credentials / access

See `SETUP.md` for the full list. Quick pointers: GCP project id and Vertex
setup mirror `core-decor-automation` (see that repo's `llms.txt` for the
working WIF/service-account pattern if auth needs re-deriving). Buffer
API key + channel IDs are GitHub Actions secrets only, NOT available in a
local shell — `tools/publish_now.py` / the `Publish Now` workflow is the
way to post a specific already-committed video without them locally.
Character/icon art generation (ChatGPT) is a fully manual, outside-the-
pipeline step — no API key stored anywhere in this repo for it; a human
pastes the prompt into ChatGPT and hands the resulting sheet back.
